ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Severe abdominal pain

A 32-year-old woman taking valproate presents with persistent severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and repeated vomiting. Lipase is markedly elevated. Ultrasound shows no gallstones and she does not drink alcohol. Which drug complication must be considered?

  1. Benign urine discoloration
  2. Valproate-associated acute pancreatitis
  3. Simple expected appetite stimulation
  4. Isolated gingival hyperplasia
  5. Drug-induced hypothyroidism
Answer and explanation

Valproate-associated acute pancreatitis

Valproate can cause life-threatening pancreatitis; this presentation requires urgent evaluation and management.

Option explanations

Valproate-associated acute pancreatitis: Valproate can cause life-threatening pancreatitis; this presentation requires urgent evaluation and management.

Simple expected appetite stimulation: Severe pain and elevated lipase indicate more than an appetite effect.

Isolated gingival hyperplasia: This does not explain the abdominal syndrome.

Drug-induced hypothyroidism: It does not characteristically produce this lipase-positive acute syndrome.

Benign urine discoloration: This is unrelated to the findings.
